resources.string: Shows what people say in videos as text, translated, in a floating box over TikTok or any other app. It reads the phone\'s own sound, so it works with AirPods and other headphones.
Checking whether this phone has Google speech recognition…

Uses the Google speech recognition built into your phone. It\'s free, it writes the words as people speak, and the sound never leaves the phone. Each language and its translation download once, when you choose them, so captions never stop to download while you\'re scrolling. With more than one language, Clip Captions spots each video\'s language in a fraction of a second and tells Google, which is much quicker than Google working it out (this needs a one-off 31 MB download).

Whisper recognises any language. Tick the ones you watch and their translations download now, once, so captions never stop to download while you\'re scrolling. A language you haven\'t ticked still works: it\'s shown in English straight away if you read English, otherwise in its own words until its translation has downloaded in the background.
Vosk, word by word (for phones without Google speech)
Automatic detection can\'t run on this phone, so choose the language below.

Bigger speech models are more accurate but slower. Automatic times each one once on this phone and uses the most accurate one that keeps captions quick. It also steps down by itself if captions start falling behind.

1. Choose how to listen (Google is the quickest), tick the languages you watch, and choose the language you want to read.
2. Tap Start captions. The first time, allow “Display over other apps” and the sound permission, then wait for the downloads. They happen once, before captions start, never while a video is playing (Wi-Fi recommended).
3. When Android asks what to share, choose “A single app” and pick the app you'll watch, such as TikTok. Your notifications stay visible. Only the sound is used, and nothing is saved.
4. Play a video and the words appear in the floating box. Swipe to the next video and they clear. Drag the box up or down, or tap ✕ to stop.

Speech recognition and translation run on your phone. Automatic detection shows captions a few seconds after the speech; choosing the language yourself shows them word by word. Clear speech works best; loud music under the voice lowers accuracy.
